### GRI 302 Energy  
Shell’s total energy consumption in 2025 was 269 million MWh, down from 289 million MWh in 2024, primarily due to portfolio changes and greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement and transformation projects [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Of the energy consumed by facilities under Shell’s operational control (189 million MWh in 2025), 99% came from fossil sources (187 million MWh), comprising crude oil and petroleum products (40 million MWh), natural gas (108 million MWh), other fossil sources (10 million MWh), and purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from fossil sources (28 million MWh) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828]. Renewable energy consumption under operational control was 2.6 million MWh in 2025 — including 2.4 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from renewable sources, 0.03 million MWh from fuels from renewable sources (e.g., biomass, biofuels, biogas, hydrogen from renewable sources), and 0.1 million MWh from self-generated non-fuel renewable energy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Energy intensity per net revenue remained stable at 0.001 MWh/$ in both 2024 and 2025, though Shell notes this metric is not considered reliable for cross-entity or longitudinal comparison due to boundary misalignment between energy consumption (ESRS reporting boundary) and net revenue (financial control boundary) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828].

### GRI 303 Water  
Water consumption reported against Shell’s operational control boundary was 86 million cubic metres in 2025, down from 90 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_878]. Of this, approximately 72 million cubic metres (84%) was used for manufacturing oil products and chemicals, and 13 million cubic metres for oil and gas production [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_870]. In 2025, Shell consumed 8 million cubic metres of water in areas of high water stress, a reduction from 21 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Water recycled and reused amounted to 25 million cubic metres in 2025, up from 23 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Shell retired its prior commitment to reduce fresh water consumption in water-stressed areas, having met it ahead of schedule in 2022; the commitment formally ended in 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_876].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Shell’s gross Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (net of carbon credits) were 53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025, down from 58 million tonnes CO₂e in 2024 and 83 million tonnes CO₂e in the 2016 baseline year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_204][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. This reflects a 36% reduction since 2016 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29]. The 2025 reduction was driven by divestments (4.8 million tonnes), emission-reduction activities and purchase of renewable electricity (1.2 million tonnes), and changes in output (0.1 million tonnes), partly offset by acquisitions (1.4 million tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. Shell’s methane emissions intensity for operated oil and gas assets with marketed gas was 0.04% in 2025, well below its target of <0.2% and consistent with its ambition to achieve near-zero intensity by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]. Routine flaring from upstream operations was eliminated in January 2025, independent of the March 2025 sale of SPDC [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Shell disposed of 1,987 thousand tonnes of waste, up from 1,933 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_278][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. This comprised 1,533 thousand tonnes of non-hazardous waste (up from 1,396 thousand tonnes) and 454 thousand tonnes of hazardous waste (down from 536 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Hazardous waste diverted from disposal totalled 207 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 409 thousand tonnes in 2024; non-hazardous waste diverted from disposal totalled 340 thousand tonnes, down from 536 thousand tonnes [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Overall, 403 thousand tonnes of residual materials were diverted for reuse, recycling or use as raw material in another process in 2025, compared with 728 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Shell’s climate strategy is anchored in its ambition to become a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050 (Scope 1, 2 and 3), with interim targets aligned to a 1.5°C pathway derived from IPCC AR6 scenarios [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_222][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165]. Key metrics include: (i) a 50% reduction in net Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 vs. 2016 (53 million tonnes CO₂e achieved in 2025, −36% vs. baseline) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_224][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]; (ii) a 15–20% reduction in net carbon intensity (NCI) of energy products sold by 2030 vs. 2016 (−9.0% achieved in 2025, baseline 78 gCO₂e/MJ) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]; and (iii) a 15–20% reduction in customer emissions from oil product use (Scope 3, Category 11) by 2030 vs. 2021 (−17.9% achieved in 2025, baseline 569 million tonnes CO₂e) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223]. Risk management integrates portfolio changes, abatement projects (e.g., CCS, electrification), and high-quality carbon credits as a last-resort compensation measure within the carbon mitigation hierarchy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223].

### Not covered in source material  
The provided context does not disclose: (i) Scope 2 emissions calculated using the location-based method separately from market-based; (ii) water discharge volumes or pollutant concentrations by medium (e.g., surface water, groundwater); (iii) waste generation or diversion rates by specific material type (e.g., plastics, metals, organics); (iv) detailed methodology or uncertainty assessment for Scope 3 Category 11 emissions beyond sales-volume-based estimation; (v) TCFD-aligned scenario analysis outputs (e.g., financial impact assessments under different climate scenarios); or (vi) governance structures specifically dedicated to water or waste risk oversight.

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures in 2025, with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025 (unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8), resulting in an FPI frequency (FPI-F) of 2.1 cases per 100 million working hours, up from 1.7 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) was 1.2 per million working hours in 2025, compared to 1.1 in 2024; lost time injury frequency (LTIF) was 0.6 per million working hours in 2025, versus 0.5 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 and Mode 2 contractual arrangements—where Shell retains control or shared interface management—but exclude Mode 3 contractors unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. Shell adopts the IOGP FPI definition, which includes outcomes where a worker cannot return to their pre-incident whole-person function due to an acute, single incident [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This reflects a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily attributable to lower employee headcount [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. Mandatory ethics and compliance training—including Code of Conduct training—was required for all employees and contractor staff [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. For roles at higher risk of corruption or bribery, 98% of staff held valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training as of 2025 (consistent with 98% in 2024), with training validity cycles set at two to three years [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. Shell also offered free anti-bribery and anti-corruption training to selected suppliers in 14 languages [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960].

### Diversity  
As of December 31, 2025, women constituted 35% of Shell’s total workforce of 85,000 employees [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Women represented 42% of the Board of Directors and 44% of the Executive Committee [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. In senior leadership positions (defined by compensation grade), women accounted for 35%—meeting Shell’s 2025 target—and Shell aims to reach 40% by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. Ethnic minority representation in UK-based Senior Management stood at 16% as of end-2025, exceeding the Parker Review’s 15% target ahead of schedule; Shell has since raised its ambition to 17% by 2027 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. Among external hires in 2025, 35% were women [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268].

### Supplier Social Assessment  
Shell’s Supplier Principles require suppliers to uphold human rights—including prohibition of child and forced labour, freedom of association, non-discrimination, safe working conditions, and fair wages—and to provide workers with confidential grievance mechanisms [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_929]. In 2025, no cases of non-respect of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines were identified in Shell’s upstream or downstream value chain [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. Similarly, no severe human rights incidents related to value chain workers were identified in 2025 (compared to three in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939]. Shell conducts risk-based pre-contractual screening and requires suppliers to flow down equivalent standards to their direct suppliers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930].

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403: No data provided on occupational health management systems, exposure assessments, or health surveillance programmes.  
GRI 404: No breakdown of training hours by topic (e.g., safety, DE&I), nor data on training effectiveness or participation rates beyond mandatory courses.  
GRI 405: No disclosure on disability inclusion metrics, LGBT+ representation, or intersectional diversity (e.g., gender × ethnicity).  
GRI 414: No quantitative data on supplier assessment coverage rate, percentage of high-risk suppliers assessed, or remediation timelines.  
TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition): No explicit analysis of workforce transitions, reskilling for low-carbon roles, community impacts of portfolio changes (e.g., divestments in Nigeria, UK, Singapore), or just transition commitments.

Governance.draft:
### Governance Structure and Board Oversight  
Shell plc’s governance framework is structured around the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee (EC), with the Board comprising 12 members—including two executive and 10 non-executive directors—as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 12 members, 2 executive and 10 non-executive members) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. All non-executive directors are considered independent in character and judgement, representing 83% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 83%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Board maintains primary oversight of Shell’s strategy—including its Energy Transition Strategy 2024, endorsed in March 2024—and monitors performance against longer-term business targets, including climate-related ambitions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Sustainability matters, including climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, are reviewed and addressed on an integrated basis alongside other business issues throughout the year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. The Board delegates authority for operational management to the CEO, who chairs the EC and is supported by EC members in implementing strategy and monitoring progress [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242].

### Board Diversity, Composition and Succession  
Shell’s Board Diversity Policy—first published in March 2024—commits to gender balance, with women constituting 42% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 42%), corresponding to a female-to-male ratio of 0.7 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Policy sets a target to maintain representation of both men and women at or above 40%, and aims to have at least one senior Board position (Chair, CEO, Senior Independent Director or CFO) held by a woman [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. Shell also aims to maintain or exceed having at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The Nomination and Succession Committee (NOMCO) oversees development of a diverse pipeline for Board succession and ensures all appointments follow a formal, rigorous and transparent procedure based on merit and objective criteria, with due regard for diversity factors [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. NOMCO engages independent executive search consultants aligned with Shell’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) approach to identify candidates from diverse pools [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379].

### Ethics, Compliance and Anti-Corruption Governance  
Accountability for ethics and compliance rests with the CEO and the Executive Committee, supported by the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO), who reports to the Chief Legal Officer and provides updates to the EC and Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Shell’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption programme includes mandatory Code of Conduct training for all employees and contractor staff, with additional targeted training for roles at higher risk of corruption exposure—such as procurement, new business development and engagement with government officials [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. In 2025, 98% of staff in at-risk roles possessed valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training completion (2024: 98%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No Shell legal entity and, to the best of Shell’s knowledge, no Shell staff were convicted or fined for criminal violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws in 2025 (2024: none) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961]. Alleged breaches may be reported confidentially—including anonymously—via the Shell Global Helpline; in 2025, 1,983 reports were received [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. Shell maintains a stringent no-retaliation policy for good-faith reporters and those participating in investigations [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_956].

### Climate and Sustainability Risk Oversight  
Climate-related risk governance is embedded across multiple Board-level committees: the Sustainability Committee oversees emerging sustainability trends (excluding carbon and safety); the Audit and Risk Committee reviews risk management effectiveness and internal controls; the Carbon Reporting Committee governs GHG emissions calculation methodologies and external disclosures; and the Strategy and Investment Committee serves as the decision forum for material capital investments aligned with the energy transition [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Climate change and the energy transition are identified as material strategic risks, broken down into commercial, societal (including litigation), regulatory and physical sub-components [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168]. The Board, EC and relevant committees regularly review these risks and their impact on the Group to enable holistic risk mitigation and integration into operational decisions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Internal assurance on sustainability-related risks is provided by Shell Internal Audit and Investigations (SIAI), which advises management and the Board on internal control effectiveness [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242].

### Not covered in source material  
The source material does not disclose: (i) specific quantitative metrics on Board meeting attendance or frequency; (ii) details of Board evaluations beyond the annual appraisal of the Chair’s performance; (iii) remuneration-linked sustainability KPIs for non-Executive Directors; (iv) third-party assurance statements on governance disclosures; (v) board-level oversight of cybersecurity or data privacy risks; (vi) disclosure of political contributions or lobbying expenditures; (vii) detailed breakdown of ARC’s oversight of ESG-related internal controls beyond general reference; (viii) Board-level review of human rights due diligence processes per UNGP or OECD Guidelines.

Environmental.draft:
### GRI 302 Energy  
Shell’s total energy consumption in 2025 was 269 million MWh, down from 289 million MWh in 2024, primarily due to portfolio changes and greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement and transformation projects [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Of the energy consumed by facilities under Shell’s operational control (189 million MWh in 2025), 99% came from fossil sources (187 million MWh), comprising crude oil and petroleum products (40 million MWh), natural gas (108 million MWh), other fossil sources (10 million MWh), and purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from fossil sources (28 million MWh) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828]. Renewable energy consumption under operational control was 2.6 million MWh in 2025 — including 2.4 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from renewable sources, 0.03 million MWh from fuels from renewable sources (e.g., biomass, biofuels, biogas, hydrogen from renewable sources), and 0.1 million MWh from self-generated non-fuel renewable energy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Energy intensity per net revenue remained stable at 0.001 MWh/$ in both 2024 and 2025, though Shell notes this metric is not considered reliable for cross-entity or longitudinal comparison due to boundary misalignment between energy consumption (ESRS reporting boundary) and net revenue (financial control boundary) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828].

### GRI 303 Water  
Water consumption reported against Shell’s operational control boundary was 86 million cubic metres in 2025, down from 90 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_878]. Of this, approximately 72 million cubic metres (84%) was used for manufacturing oil products and chemicals, and 13 million cubic metres for oil and gas production [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_870]. In 2025, Shell consumed 8 million cubic metres of water in areas of high water stress, a reduction from 21 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Water recycled and reused amounted to 25 million cubic metres in 2025, up from 23 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Shell retired its prior commitment to reduce fresh water consumption in water-stressed areas, having met it ahead of schedule in 2022; the commitment formally ended in 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_876].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Shell’s gross Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (net of carbon credits) were 53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025, down from 58 million tonnes CO₂e in 2024 and 83 million tonnes CO₂e in the 2016 baseline year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_204][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. This reflects a 36% reduction since 2016 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29]. The 2025 reduction was driven by divestments (4.8 million tonnes), emission-reduction activities and purchase of renewable electricity (1.2 million tonnes), and changes in output (0.1 million tonnes), partly offset by acquisitions (1.4 million tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. Shell’s methane emissions intensity for operated oil and gas assets with marketed gas was 0.04% in 2025, well below its target of <0.2% and consistent with its ambition to achieve near-zero intensity by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]. Routine flaring from upstream operations was eliminated in January 2025, independent of the March 2025 sale of SPDC [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Shell disposed of 1,987 thousand tonnes of waste, up from 1,933 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_278][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. This comprised 1,533 thousand tonnes of non-hazardous waste (up from 1,396 thousand tonnes) and 454 thousand tonnes of hazardous waste (down from 536 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Hazardous waste diverted from disposal totalled 207 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 409 thousand tonnes in 2024; non-hazardous waste diverted from disposal totalled 340 thousand tonnes, down from 536 thousand tonnes [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Overall, 403 thousand tonnes of residual materials were diverted for reuse, recycling or use as raw material in another process in 2025, compared with 728 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Shell’s climate strategy is anchored in its ambition to become a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050 (Scope 1, 2 and 3), with interim targets aligned to a 1.5°C pathway derived from IPCC AR6 scenarios [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_222][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165]. Key metrics include: (i) a 50% reduction in net Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 vs. 2016 (53 million tonnes CO₂e achieved in 2025, −36% vs. baseline) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_224][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]; (ii) a 15–20% reduction in net carbon intensity (NCI) of energy products sold by 2030 vs. 2016 (−9.0% achieved in 2025, baseline 78 gCO₂e/MJ) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]; and (iii) a 15–20% reduction in customer emissions from oil product use (Scope 3, Category 11) by 2030 vs. 2021 (−17.9% achieved in 2025, baseline 569 million tonnes CO₂e) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223]. Risk management integrates portfolio changes, abatement projects (e.g., CCS, electrification), and high-quality carbon credits as a last-resort compensation measure within the carbon mitigation hierarchy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223].

### Not covered in source material  
The provided context does not disclose: (i) Scope 2 emissions calculated using the location-based method separately from market-based; (ii) water discharge volumes or pollutant concentrations by medium (e.g., surface water, groundwater); (iii) waste generation or diversion rates by specific material type (e.g., plastics, metals, organics); (iv) detailed methodology or uncertainty assessment for Scope 3 Category 11 emissions beyond sales-volume-based estimation; (v) TCFD-aligned scenario analysis outputs (e.g., financial impact assessments under different climate scenarios); or (vi) governance structures specifically dedicated to water or waste risk oversight.

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures in 2025, with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025, unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. However, the FPI frequency (FPI-F) increased to 2.1 cases per 100 million working hours in 2025, up from 1.7 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. This increase reflects a reduction in total working hours — consistent with the 13% decline in total headcount (from 96,000 at end-2024 to 85,000 at end-2025) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921] — though the exact denominator (total working hours) is not disclosed in the source material. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) rose marginally to 1.2 per million working hours in 2025 (from 1.1 in 2024), and lost time injury frequency (LTIF) increased to 0.6 per million working hours (from 0.5 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 and Mode 2 contractual arrangements — where Shell retains control or shared interface management — but exclude Mode 3 contractors unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. Shell adopts the IOGP definition of FPI as “the outcome of a work-related injury from which the worker cannot or is not expected to return to their previous pre-incident whole person function as a result of an acute, single incident” [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974]. No information is provided on occupational health management systems (e.g., ISO 45001 certification status), exposure assessments, health surveillance programmes, or frequency of medical monitoring for high-risk roles [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This represents a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily attributable to lower employee headcount [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. Mandatory ethics and compliance training — including Code of Conduct training — was required for all employees and contractor staff [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. For roles identified as being at higher risk of corruption or bribery, 98% of staff held valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training as of 2025 (consistent with 98% in 2024), with training validity cycles set at two to three years [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. Shell also offered free anti-bribery and anti-corruption training to selected suppliers in 14 languages [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No data is provided on training participation rates by course type (mandatory vs. voluntary), topic-specific breakdowns (e.g., safety, DE&I, climate transition), competency validation, or correlation between training and safety/incident outcomes [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960].

### Diversity  
As of December 31, 2025, women constituted 35% of Shell’s total workforce of 85,000 employees [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Women represented 42% of the Board of Directors and 44% of the Executive Committee [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. In senior leadership positions (defined by compensation grade), women accounted for 35% — meeting Shell’s 2025 target — and Shell aims to reach 40% by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. Ethnic minority representation in UK-based Senior Management stood at 16% as of end-2025, exceeding the Parker Review’s 15% target ahead of schedule; Shell has since raised its ambition to 17% by 2027 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. Among external hires in 2025, 35% were women [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. No data is provided on disability employment rate, reasonable accommodation requests, LGBT+ representation, employee resource group participation, or intersectional metrics (e.g., gender × ethnicity or gender × age) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268].

### Supplier Social Assessment  
Shell’s Supplier Principles require suppliers to uphold human rights — including prohibition of child and forced labour, freedom of association, non-discrimination, safe working conditions, fair wages, and provision of confidential grievance mechanisms — and to flow down equivalent standards to their direct suppliers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_929]. In 2025, no cases of non-respect of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines were identified in Shell’s upstream or downstream value chain [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. Similarly, no severe human rights incidents related to value chain workers were identified in 2025 (compared to three in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939]. The source material does not define “severe” using GRI 414-2 or UN Guiding Principles criteria (e.g., forced labour, fatal accidents, systemic discrimination), nor does it disclose the number or type of supplier assessments conducted (e.g., desktop reviews, on-site audits), coverage of procurement spend, or audit depth thresholds applied [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939].

### TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition)  
The source material notes that Shell’s portfolio changes — including divestments in Singapore (Bukom, Jurong), Nigeria (SPDC), and the UK (to the Adura joint venture) — contributed to the reduction in headcount from 96,000 in 2024 to 85,000 in 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_261]. It further states that Shell is transforming to “deliver more value with less emissions” and that “as we reshape our portfolio, elements of our culture will need to adapt”, including developing new skills and adapting processes for emerging businesses [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_910][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_913]. However, no quantitative data is provided on reskilling investments, displaced worker support programmes (e.g., severance, retraining, outplacement), or community impact assessments related to divested assets [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_913].

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403: No disclosure of occupational health management system scope, certification status (e.g., ISO 45001), exposure assessments, or health surveillance frequency for high-risk roles.  
GRI 404: No breakdown of training by topic (e.g., safety, DE&I, climate transition), no training participation rates by mandatory vs. voluntary courses, and no effectiveness metrics (e.g., competency validation, incident reduction correlation).  
GRI 405: No data on disability employment rate, reasonable accommodation requests, LGBT+ representation, employee resource group participation, or intersectional diversity metrics.  
GRI 414: No disclosure of total Tier 1 suppliers, number of suppliers assessed in 2025, percentage of high-risk suppliers fully evaluated, or methodology used to determine “severe” human rights incidents.  
TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition): No quantification of reskilling investments, no description of just transition commitments, no community impact assessments for divested assets (e.g., Nigeria, UK, Singapore), and no data on support for workers affected by portfolio changes.

Governance.draft:
### Governance Structure and Board Oversight  
Shell plc’s governance framework is structured around the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee (EC), with the Board comprising 12 members—including two executive and 10 non-executive directors—as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 12 members, 2 executive and 10 non-executive members) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. All non-executive directors are considered independent in character and judgement, representing 83% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 83%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Board maintains primary oversight of Shell’s strategy—including its Energy Transition Strategy 2024, endorsed in March 2024—and monitors performance against longer-term business targets, including climate-related ambitions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Sustainability matters, including climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, are reviewed and addressed on an integrated basis alongside other business issues throughout the year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. The Board delegates authority for operational management to the CEO, who chairs the EC and is supported by EC members in implementing strategy and monitoring progress [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. This structure aligns with GRI 2-11 (governance bodies’ roles and responsibilities) and TCFD Governance (g1–g4), as the Board explicitly oversees strategy, risk, and sustainability integration across time horizons defined as short term (one year), medium term (2–10 years), and long term (beyond 10 years) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_754].

### Board Diversity, Composition and Succession  
Shell’s Board Diversity Policy—first published in March 2024—commits to gender balance, with women constituting 42% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 42%), corresponding to a female-to-male ratio of 0.7 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Policy sets a target to maintain representation of both men and women at or above 40%, and aims to have at least one senior Board position (Chair, CEO, Senior Independent Director or CFO) held by a woman [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The source material does not disclose the baseline year for this senior-position target, nor whether it has been achieved as of December 31, 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. Shell also aims to maintain or exceed having at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]; however, the absolute number and percentage of Board members from minority ethnic backgrounds for 2025 and 2024 are not disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The Nomination and Succession Committee (NOMCO) oversees development of a diverse pipeline for Board succession and ensures all appointments follow a formal, rigorous and transparent procedure based on merit and objective criteria, with due regard for diversity factors [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. NOMCO engages independent executive search consultants aligned with Shell’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) approach to identify candidates from diverse pools [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. The 2025 Board Performance Review was externally facilitated by Jan Hall of No. 4 through one-on-one interviews with all Board members, the Company Secretary, External Audit partner, and three EC members, supplemented by observation of Board and Committee meetings and review of pre-meeting materials [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_370]. The review was conducted in January 2026 and covered effectiveness, dynamics, and alignment with the UK Corporate Governance Code requirement for triennial external evaluation [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_370]. No outcomes, findings, or remediation actions from the 2025 review are disclosed in the source material [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_370].

### Ethics, Compliance and Anti-Corruption Governance  
Accountability for ethics and compliance rests with the CEO and the Executive Committee, supported by the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO), who reports to the Chief Legal Officer and provides updates to the EC and Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Shell’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption programme includes mandatory Code of Conduct training for all employees and contractor staff, with additional targeted training for roles at higher risk of corruption exposure—such as procurement, new business development and engagement with government officials [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. In 2025, 98% of staff in at-risk roles possessed valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training completion (2024: 98%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No Shell legal entity and, to the best of Shell’s knowledge, no Shell staff were convicted or fined for criminal violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws in 2025 (2024: none) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961]. Alleged breaches may be reported confidentially—including anonymously—via the Shell Global Helpline; in 2025, 1,983 reports were received [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. The source material does not disclose the number or percentage of Helpline reports substantiated, closed, or under investigation in 2025, nor any 2024 comparison [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. Shell maintains a stringent no-retaliation policy for good-faith reporters and those participating in investigations [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_956]. This fulfils GRI 205-1 (anti-corruption policy), GRI 205-2 (training coverage), and GRI 205-3 (incidents and enforcement), though quantitative resolution metrics are absent.

### Climate and Sustainability Risk Oversight  
Climate-related risk governance is embedded across multiple Board-level committees: the Sustainability Committee oversees emerging sustainability trends (excluding carbon and safety); the Audit and Risk Committee reviews risk management effectiveness and internal controls; the Carbon Reporting Committee governs GHG emissions calculation methodologies and external disclosures; and the Strategy and Investment Committee serves as the decision forum for material capital investments aligned with the energy transition [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Climate change and the energy transition are identified as material strategic risks, broken down into commercial, societal (including litigation), regulatory and physical sub-components [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168]. The Board, EC and relevant committees regularly review these risks and their impact on the Group to enable holistic risk mitigation and integration into operational decisions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Internal assurance on sustainability-related risks is provided by Shell Internal Audit and Investigations (SIAI), which advises management and the Board on internal control effectiveness [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. The source material does not disclose Board or committee responsibility for oversight of cybersecurity, data privacy, or human rights due diligence—including frequency, scope, or methodology of review [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Nor does it disclose specific, measurable governance targets (e.g., committee review frequency, assurance coverage scope) tied to Energy Transition Strategy 2024 implementation [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759].

### Not covered in source material  
The source material does not disclose: (i) political contributions or lobbying expenditures, nor any explanation for their absence; (ii) whether any Board diversity or ethics training targets were missed in 2025 and why; (iii) trend data showing a negative or stagnant governance metric (e.g., Helpline resolution rate decline) with root-cause analysis; (iv) board-level oversight of cybersecurity or data privacy risks; (v) board-level review of human rights due diligence processes per UNGP or OECD Guidelines; (vi) remuneration-linked sustainability KPIs for non-Executive Directors; (vii) third-party assurance statements on governance disclosures; (viii) the baseline year or current status of the target for “at least one senior Board position held by a woman”; (ix) the absolute number and percentage of Board members from minority ethnic backgrounds for 2025 and 2024; (x) the number and percentage of Shell Global Helpline reports substantiated, closed, or under investigation in 2025, with 2024 comparison; (xi) specific deadlines for Board diversity targets; (xii) quantitative data on political contributions and lobbying expenditures; (xiii) methodology or results of committee-level evaluations beyond the Board Performance Review; (xiv) disclosure of challenges preventing political contribution reporting. These omissions correspond to gaps in GRI 2-12 (board evaluation process), GRI 2-13 (remuneration linkages), and TCFD Governance (g1–g4) requirements for comprehensive oversight scope and forward-looking targets.

### GRI 302 Energy  
Shell’s total energy consumption in 2025 was 269 million MWh, down from 289 million MWh in 2024, primarily due to portfolio changes and greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement and transformation projects [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Of the energy consumed by facilities under Shell’s operational control (189 million MWh in 2025), 99% came from fossil sources (187 million MWh), comprising crude oil and petroleum products (40 million MWh), natural gas (108 million MWh), other fossil sources (10 million MWh), and purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from fossil sources (28 million MWh) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828]. Renewable energy consumption under operational control was 2.6 million MWh in 2025 — including 2.4 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from renewable sources, 0.03 million MWh from fuels from renewable sources (e.g., biomass, biofuels, biogas, hydrogen from renewable sources), and 0.1 million MWh from self-generated non-fuel renewable energy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Energy intensity per net revenue remained stable at 0.001 MWh/$ in both 2024 and 2025, though Shell notes this metric is not considered reliable for cross-entity or longitudinal comparison due to boundary misalignment between energy consumption (ESRS reporting boundary) and net revenue (financial control boundary) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828].

### GRI 303 Water  
Water consumption reported against Shell’s operational control boundary was 86 million cubic metres in 2025, down from 90 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_878]. Of this, approximately 72 million cubic metres (84%) was used for manufacturing oil products and chemicals, and 13 million cubic metres for oil and gas production [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_870]. In 2025, Shell consumed 8 million cubic metres of water in areas of high water stress, a reduction from 21 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Water recycled and reused amounted to 25 million cubic metres in 2025, up from 23 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Shell retired its prior commitment to reduce fresh water consumption in water-stressed areas, having met it ahead of schedule in 2022; the commitment formally ended in 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_876].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Shell’s gross Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (net of carbon credits) were 53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025, down from 58 million tonnes CO₂e in 2024 and 83 million tonnes CO₂e in the 2016 baseline year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_204][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. This reflects a 36% reduction since 2016 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29]. The 2025 reduction was driven by divestments (4.8 million tonnes), emission-reduction activities and purchase of renewable electricity (1.2 million tonnes), and changes in output (0.1 million tonnes), partly offset by acquisitions (1.4 million tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. Shell’s methane emissions intensity for operated oil and gas assets with marketed gas was 0.04% in 2025, well below its target of <0.2% and consistent with its ambition to achieve near-zero intensity by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]. Routine flaring from upstream operations was eliminated in January 2025, independent of the March 2025 sale of SPDC [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Shell disposed of 1,987 thousand tonnes of waste, up from 1,933 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_278][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. This comprised 1,533 thousand tonnes of non-hazardous waste (up from 1,396 thousand tonnes) and 454 thousand tonnes of hazardous waste (down from 536 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Hazardous waste diverted from disposal totalled 207 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 409 thousand tonnes in 2024; non-hazardous waste diverted from disposal totalled 340 thousand tonnes, down from 536 thousand tonnes [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Overall, 403 thousand tonnes of residual materials were diverted for reuse, recycling or use as raw material in another process in 2025, compared with 728 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Shell’s climate strategy is anchored in its ambition to become a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050 (Scope 1, 2 and 3), with interim targets aligned to a 1.5°C pathway derived from IPCC AR6 scenarios [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_222][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165]. Key metrics include: (i) a 50% reduction in net Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 vs. 2016 (53 million tonnes CO₂e achieved in 2025, −36% vs. baseline) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_224][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]; (ii) a 15–20% reduction in net carbon intensity (NCI) of energy products sold by 2030 vs. 2016 (−9.0% achieved in 2025, baseline 78 gCO₂e/MJ) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]; and (iii) a 15–20% reduction in customer emissions from oil product use (Scope 3, Category 11) by 2030 vs. 2021 (−17.9% achieved in 2025, baseline 569 million tonnes CO₂e) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223]. Risk management integrates portfolio changes, abatement projects (e.g., CCS, electrification), and high-quality carbon credits as a last-resort compensation measure within the carbon mitigation hierarchy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223].

### Not covered in source material  
The provided context does not disclose: (i) Scope 2 emissions calculated using the location-based method separately from market-based; (ii) water discharge volumes or pollutant concentrations by medium (e.g., surface water, groundwater); (iii) waste generation or diversion rates by specific material type (e.g., plastics, metals, organics); (iv) detailed methodology or uncertainty assessment for Scope 3 Category 11 emissions beyond sales-volume-based estimation; (v) TCFD-aligned scenario analysis outputs (e.g., financial impact assessments under different climate scenarios); or (vi) governance structures specifically dedicated to water or waste risk oversight.

### Occupational Health & Safety  
In 2025, Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures — one in Malaysia (EcoOils facility), one in Malaysia (mobile drilling rig), one in Argentina (road traffic incident), and one in the North Sea (fall from height) — with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025, unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. FPI is defined by Shell as “the outcome of a work-related injury from which the worker cannot or is not expected to return to their previous pre-incident whole person function as a result of an acute, single incident”, consistent with IOGP metrics [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974]. The FPI frequency (FPI-F) increased to 2.1 cases per 100 million working hours in 2025, up from 1.7 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) rose to 1.2 per million working hours (from 1.1 in 2024), and lost time injury frequency (LTIF) increased to 0.6 per million working hours (from 0.5 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 (Shell-controlled workplace) and Mode 2 (shared interface management) contractual arrangements; Mode 3 contractors are excluded unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. The source material does not disclose total working hours for 2024 or 2025, nor does it state whether the rise in LTIF/TRCF reflects operational changes, reporting refinements, or emerging risks [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. No information is provided on occupational health management systems (e.g., ISO 45001 certification status or scope), exposure assessments, health surveillance programmes, or medical monitoring frequency for high-risk roles [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This represents a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily attributable to lower employee headcount (85,000 at end-2025 vs. 96,000 at end-2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Mandatory ethics and compliance training — including Code of Conduct training — was required for all employees and contractor staff [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. For roles identified as being at higher risk of corruption or bribery, 98% of staff held valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training as of 2025 (consistent with 98% in 2024), with training validity cycles set at two to three years [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. Shell also offered free anti-bribery and anti-corruption training to selected suppliers in 14 languages [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. The source material does not disclose training participation rates by course type (mandatory vs. voluntary), breakdowns by topic (e.g., safety, DE&I, climate transition), competency validation methods, or correlation between training and safety/incident outcomes [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960].

### Diversity  
As of December 31, 2025, women constituted 35% of Shell’s total workforce of 85,000 employees [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Women represented 42% of the Board of Directors and 44% of the Executive Committee [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. In senior leadership positions (defined by compensation grade), women accounted for 35% — meeting Shell’s 2025 target — and Shell aims to reach 40% by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. Ethnic minority representation in UK-based Senior Management stood at 16% as of end-2025, exceeding the Parker Review’s 15% target ahead of schedule; Shell has since raised its ambition to 17% by 2027 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. Among external hires in 2025, 35% were women [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. The source material states that Shell offers employees the option to voluntarily declare race and ethnicity via a self-identification initiative but does not report disability employment rate, reasonable accommodation request volume or resolution rate, LGBT+ representation, employee resource group participation, or intersectional metrics (e.g., gender × ethnicity or gender × age) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_269][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378].

### Supplier Social Assessment  
Shell’s Supplier Principles require suppliers to uphold human rights — including prohibition of child and forced labour, freedom of association, non-discrimination, safe working conditions, fair wages, and provision of confidential grievance mechanisms — and to flow down equivalent standards to their direct suppliers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_929]. In 2025, no cases of non-respect of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines were identified in Shell’s upstream or downstream value chain [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. Similarly, no severe human rights incidents related to value chain workers were identified in 2025 (compared to three in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939]. However, the source material does not define “severe human rights incident” using GRI 414-2 criteria (e.g., forced labour, fatal accidents, systemic discrimination), nor does it disclose the number or type of supplier assessments conducted (e.g., desktop reviews, on-site audits), coverage of procurement spend, audit depth thresholds, or absolute count and percentage of Tier 1 suppliers assessed against Shell’s Supplier Principles in 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939].

### TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition)  
The source material notes that Shell’s portfolio changes — including divestments in Singapore (Bukom, Jurong), Nigeria (SPDC), and the UK (to the Adura joint venture) — contributed to the reduction in headcount from 96,000 in 2024 to 85,000 in 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_261]. It further states that Shell is transforming to “deliver more value with less emissions” and that “as we reshape our portfolio, elements of our culture will need to adapt”, including developing new skills and adapting processes for emerging businesses [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_910][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_913]. However, no quantitative data is provided on reskilling investments, displaced worker support programmes (e.g., severance, retraining, outplacement), community impact assessments related to divested assets, or just transition commitments [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_913].

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403: No disclosure of occupational health management system scope, certification status (e.g., ISO 45001), exposure assessments, health surveillance frequency for high-risk roles, or total working hours for 2024 and 2025.  
GRI 404: No breakdown of training days by topic (e.g., safety, DE&I, climate transition), no distinction between mandatory and voluntary participation rates, and no effectiveness metrics (e.g., competency validation, incident reduction correlation).  
GRI 405: No disclosure of disability employment rate, reasonable accommodation request volume or resolution rate, LGBT+ representation, employee resource group participation, or intersectional diversity metrics (e.g., gender × ethnicity, gender × age).  
GRI 414: No definition of “severe human rights incident” aligned with GRI 414-2 criteria; no count or categorisation of incidents (e.g., forced labour, fatal accident, systemic discrimination); no disclosure of total Tier 1 suppliers, number of suppliers assessed in 2025, percentage of high-risk suppliers fully evaluated, or methodology used to determine assessment depth.  
TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition): No quantification of annual reskilling investment, no description of just transition commitments, no community impact assessments for divested assets (e.g., Nigeria, UK, Singapore), and no data on support for workers affected by portfolio changes (e.g., outplacement, retraining, severance).

### Governance Structure and Board Oversight  
Shell plc’s governance framework is structured around the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee (EC), with the Board comprising 12 members—including two executive and 10 non-executive directors—as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 12 members, 2 executive and 10 non-executive members) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. All non-executive directors are considered independent in character and judgement, representing 83% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 83%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Board maintains primary oversight of Shell’s strategy—including its Energy Transition Strategy 2024, endorsed in March 2024—and monitors performance against longer-term business targets, including climate-related ambitions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Sustainability matters, including climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, are reviewed and addressed on an integrated basis alongside other business issues throughout the year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. The Board delegates authority for operational management to the CEO, who chairs the EC and is supported by EC members in implementing strategy and monitoring progress [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. This structure aligns with GRI 2-11 (governance bodies’ roles and responsibilities) and TCFD Governance (g1–g4), as the Board explicitly oversees strategy, risk, and sustainability integration across time horizons defined as short term (one year), medium term (2–10 years), and long term (beyond 10 years) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_754].

### Board Diversity, Composition and Succession  
Shell’s Board Diversity Policy—first published in March 2024—commits to gender balance, with women constituting 42% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 42%), corresponding to a female-to-male ratio of 0.7 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Policy sets a target to maintain representation of both men and women at or above 40%, and aims to have at least one senior Board position (Chair, CEO, Senior Independent Director or CFO) held by a woman [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The source material does not disclose the baseline year for this senior-position target, nor whether it has been achieved as of December 31, 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. Shell also aims to maintain or exceed having at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]; however, the absolute number and percentage of Board members from minority ethnic backgrounds for 2025 and 2024 are not disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The Nomination and Succession Committee (NOMCO) oversees development of a diverse pipeline for Board succession and ensures all appointments follow a formal, rigorous and transparent procedure based on merit and objective criteria, with due regard for diversity factors [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. NOMCO engages independent executive search consultants aligned with Shell’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) approach to identify candidates from diverse pools [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. The 2025 Board Performance Review was externally facilitated by Jan Hall of No. 4 through one-on-one interviews with all Board members, the Company Secretary, External Audit partner, and three EC members, supplemented by observation of Board and Committee meetings and review of pre-meeting materials [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_370]. The review was conducted in January 2026 and covered effectiveness, dynamics, and alignment with the UK Corporate Governance Code requirement for triennial external evaluation [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_370]. No outcomes, findings, or remediation actions from the 2025 review are disclosed in the source material [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_370].

### Ethics, Compliance and Anti-Corruption Governance  
Accountability for ethics and compliance rests with the CEO and the Executive Committee, supported by the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO), who reports to the Chief Legal Officer and provides updates to the EC and Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Shell’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption programme includes mandatory Code of Conduct training for all employees and contractor staff, with additional targeted training for roles at higher risk of corruption exposure—such as procurement, new business development and engagement with government officials [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. In 2025, 98% of staff in at-risk roles possessed valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training completion (2024: 98%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No Shell legal entity and, to the best of Shell’s knowledge, no Shell staff were convicted or fined for criminal violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws in 2025 (2024: none) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961]. Alleged breaches may be reported confidentially—including anonymously—via the Shell Global Helpline; in 2025, 1,983 reports were received [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. The source material does not disclose the number or percentage of Helpline reports substantiated, closed, or under investigation in 2025, nor any 2024 comparison [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. Shell maintains a stringent no-retaliation policy for good-faith reporters and those participating in investigations [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_956]. This fulfils GRI 205-1 (anti-corruption policy), GRI 205-2 (training coverage), and GRI 205-3 (incidents and enforcement), though quantitative resolution metrics are absent.

### Climate and Sustainability Risk Oversight  
Climate-related risk governance is embedded across multiple Board-level committees: the Sustainability Committee oversees emerging sustainability trends (excluding carbon and safety); the Audit and Risk Committee reviews risk management effectiveness and internal controls; the Carbon Reporting Committee governs GHG emissions calculation methodologies and external disclosures; and the Strategy and Investment Committee serves as the decision forum for material capital investments aligned with the energy transition [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Climate change and the energy transition are identified as material strategic risks, broken down into commercial, societal (including litigation), regulatory and physical sub-components [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168]. The Board, EC and relevant committees regularly review these risks and their impact on the Group to enable holistic risk mitigation and integration into operational decisions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Internal assurance on sustainability-related risks is provided by Shell Internal Audit and Investigations (SIAI), which advises management and the Board on internal control effectiveness [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. The source material does not disclose Board or committee responsibility for oversight of cybersecurity, data privacy, or human rights due diligence—including frequency, scope, or methodology of review [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. Nor does it disclose specific, measurable governance targets (e.g., committee review frequency, assurance coverage scope) tied to Energy Transition Strategy 2024 implementation [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759].

### Not covered in source material  
The source material does not disclose: (i) political contributions or lobbying expenditures, nor any explanation for their absence; (ii) whether any Board diversity or ethics training targets were missed in 2025 and why; (iii) trend data showing a negative or stagnant governance metric (e.g., Helpline resolution rate decline) with root-cause analysis; (iv) board-level oversight of cybersecurity or data privacy risks; (v) board-level review of human rights due diligence processes per UNGP or OECD Guidelines; (vi) remuneration-linked sustainability KPIs for non-Executive Directors; (vii) third-party assurance statements on governance disclosures; (viii) the baseline year or current status of the target for “at least one senior Board position held by a woman”; (ix) the absolute number and percentage of Board members from minority ethnic backgrounds for 2025 and 2024; (x) the number and percentage of Shell Global Helpline reports substantiated, closed, or under investigation in 2025, with 2024 comparison; (xi) specific deadlines for Board diversity targets; (xii) quantitative data on political contributions and lobbying expenditures; (xiii) methodology or results of committee-level evaluations beyond the Board Performance Review; (xiv) disclosure of challenges preventing political contribution reporting. These omissions correspond to gaps in GRI 2-12 (board evaluation process), GRI 2-13 (remuneration linkages), and TCFD Governance (g1–g4) requirements for comprehensive oversight scope and forward-looking targets.
